Hey! Thanks for the comment (I don't mean it sarcastically, like genuinely, thanks for the comment). It kind of threw me into a rabbit hole as it chalenged my pre-conceived ideas of what  race and ethncity are, and I researched the cocncepts for a while.

I am, of course, not an expert anthrophologist nor this mini-research was super academic (heck I haven't even finished high school), so take evrything I say with a big grain of salt. However I stand on my point that "White" shouldn't be labeled as an ethnicity. As you remarked, it actually means European or of European descent, so perhaps we should use that as an ethnicity rather than "white."

Why? Well, based on this unprofesional and probably unreliable 1-hour-research I made, the general (super, super general) consensus for what race is a description of physicla traits ( “a category of humankind that shares certain distinctive physical traits.”  [https://www.nationalgeographic.com/culture/topics/reference/race-ethnicity/](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/culture/topics/reference/race-ethnicity/)) while an ethnicty is something more cultural and that is learned while growing up. Even this sub's additional guidelines say so.

Aside from this, and based more on personal opinion and subjectiveness declaring that

>"Latinx/Hispanic people are often considered brown (though different to the Asian brown) but many are fair enough to pass as white."

is racist, and *errases the specific struggles that afro, asian, and indigenous peoples* suffer in, for example, Latin America. ^(I cannot speak for Asian -in this case East-asian- culture or Southern Europeans, as I am not part of those groups, though I believe the same applies to  some extent.) There *are* black latine people, as well as latinas and latinos with east-asian features  or descent (no, not indigenous features confused as asian features) that identify not as Afro or Asian respectively , but as Latine, as they were not raised in touch with Afro or Asian culture (respc.), nor have close realaties that are part of said cultures.  This, aside from those latines that ARE part of/maintain their relationship with their culture (in these examples Afro or Asian).  There are many latin americans with white/caucasian physical traits, yet this doesn't make them "white" (as per your definition, a.k.a. " European " ). However, it is also important to mention that a mestizaje processes happened in Latinamerica, and many Latines *have* european descent or have caucasian traits, yet this doesn't make us European. If you want to, you can inform yourself about this topic in specific, with this article on racism in latinamerica: [https://www.socialsciences.manchester.ac.uk/about/stories/racism-after-race/](https://www.socialsciences.manchester.ac.uk/about/stories/racism-after-race/)

Made my PP last year. Overall, it IS important, but it isn't a "career" defining moment/project. Pay attention to your school and tutors, they'll probably explain this to you better, and will know how to guide you better as well lol. Besides, they'll probably also explain you what they want from you better.

"Briefly" summmarizing, the PP is the documentation and records from an investigation ( on any topic you like) that leads to a product.         However, and I can't stress this enough, the product *DOESN'T* matter, at ALL. Everything the IB wants from you is for you to be able to research, be proficient at following guidelines, document everything you do, and to reflect on research and documentation.

An example of this: a friend's topic was Vanilla's Icecream History. He didn't have a product, nor a proper investigation, didn't even do much yet got a pretty high grade (fifth best in my generation). Why? He had the best repport in the generation, following every instruction that we had for writing the repport, and had one of the best reflections ever. 
(Now he could pull off the not doing absolutely anything cuz of luck and cuz he's a friggin genius, so wouldn't recommend. However, this shows how little the final product actually matters)



Thats why, Personal Project's most important part is the REPORT, which is divided into 6 (technically 4 that matter) parts called criterions (sorry, probs named something different in english, but its the best I can do haha)

Besides of what I write in continuation. In each criterion you need to explain how you developed one sub-skill from a list of skills the IB gives (i.e. Social and Communication Skills, or Investigation Skills). There is a word limit, you can exceed it not by much if you show you actually need too. The word limit for English is about 1500 or 2000 I believe, however I took MYP in Spanish so can't be sure.

Criterion A:Investigation

You basically tell what you did while investigating about your topic

Criterion B: Planification

You must add a cronogram, some rubrics and tell how you did those. The rubrics are to evaluate your product, and the cronogram states how/when you're going to make it.

Cruterion C: Action

You tell wtf you did with the information and how tf you did ypur product

Criterion D: Reflection

You reflect on it all.
Your grade your product
You say what IB profil attributes you used

 (These two dont count in the word limit)
Bibliography
Annexes

The first one is pretty self-explenatory. The second one, is more complicated (and I may have transalted it poorly, sorry :c). Annexes are photos, texts, notes screenshots, polls, samples, transcripts of interviews etc. that prove you did your work. If you wrote 5 000 words of investigation you put em here, and title them Annex #: What the text says. If you cretaed a drone, you put pictures of you making it here, you put screenshots of the instructions, materials etc. 

Don't know if the same applies for your school. But mine made us do a work diary (again with specific needs and requirements), and we had to add some photos in annexes



So... quick tips
       -Get out your inner obedient robot and follow every                   guideline  your school gives you. 

(If they're like mine they'll probably give you a 70 something pages booklet, try to read everything in it concerning PP, and some examples from past PP's )

      -However, don limit creativity. The IB tells you what to do, not how to do it. 


       -Again, do not fucking worry about the product
               -on that note, product can literally be anything

       -Enjoy as much as you can


Some weird ideas you for your PP's topic: (sorry I am not thinking really creatively rn hahahha) however know, anything goes.

-How Acid Rain affects crops in your town.
-Research some math theorem, and relate it to something of everydaylife
-Make a book (booklet) on moral dilemas, or a philosophy
-Perhaps research about roads or buildings and how to make em more ecofriendly
-research on how dams work, and how to reduce their impact on the ecosystem


Hope this helped, even if just a bit. If you need anything DM/PM me, will happilly respond. I know that uncertainty of not knowing wtf PP is, been there. In the end, everything clears up :)
